title: Kaiser's tonk and the New York Cafe at Howard and Rampart
summary: Interviewers ask about Kaiser's tonk and the New York Cafe, which Nash identifies as Pink Allen's barbershop under Vic Dubar's ballroom.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: It's Marshall Kaiser. He was an ex- Let me run it back for a second. I don't remember that.
Can you remember Randy? No. You don't remember Kaiser's Tonk though. He was right across from the Union Terminal.
Yeah, I remember that. Yeah, that was a little, a lot smaller though.
Yeah, it went out I think about 1907 they finally closed him for good. 1907? 1908. Closed him for good.
Do you remember the New York Cafe which was right up on Grandpa near Howard? You want to see? Just above Howard across from the station there. Up the station?
You mean Howard Avenue and Grandpa?
Well that was Pink Allen had a barbershop downstairs and they had Vic DuBarr had a ballroom upstairs.
This was on Grandpa facing the station. Facing the station?
Well that's the place he's talking about.
1945 wasn't that the start of an advertisement?
I went there with Joe Avery and Lil Patilman. I went there with the Habitizer.
I'll be, I'll be, I'll be, that's on Rampart Street between Caliope and Howard Avenue. Mm-hmm.
Yeah. Mm-hmm. I was there in that same place. A year later I met. Yes, I remember.
